summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on regulation, product + fintech innovation.

articles.title: Will Europe unseat Visa, Mastercard?
articles.description: The Wero project launched by European banks is making progress in challenging the card networks’ dominance on the continent, but the U.S. companies still have an edge, one firm’s analysts contend.

articles.title: Circle CFO to step down
articles.description: Finance chief Jeremy Fox-Geen will leave the stablecoin issuer later this year, after ushering the company through its long-awaited 2025 IPO.

articles.title: AI shopping agents need receipts
articles.description: As artificial intelligence assumes a bigger role in commerce and finances, having a clear record of agents’ actions is critical, executives said.

articles.title: Senate passes Common Cents bill
articles.description: The measure to provide merchants a cash rounding framework, and to formally phase out the penny, now heads to the White House.

articles.title: FedNow tiptoes into cross-border
articles.description: The Federal Reserve is inching toward adding some sort of cross-border capability to FedNow, but it’s not clear when or how.

articles.title: Apple lawsuit becomes class action
articles.description: The tech giant could face claims from thousands of card issuers that paid Apple Pay fees for payments made via Apple’s devices as part of a California lawsuit.

articles.title: Fed proposes stablecoin rules
articles.description: The regulations aim to make these digital assets “foster payments improvements that benefit households and businesses,” Federal Reserve Gov. Michael Barr said.

articles.title: Payment revenue growth to slow
articles.description: The rate of payments-related revenue growth in North America, and globally, will slow in the next four years, a major consulting firm predicts.
